title: A reduced planar body with area greater than $πΔ^2/4$
summary: We construct a reduced planar convex body $R$ with thickness $Δ(R)=1$ and \[\operatorname{area}(R)=0.786215\ldots>0.785398\ldots=\fracπ{4}.\] Thus $R$ is a counterexample to Lassak's conjectured upper bound $\operatorname{area}\le(π/4)Δ^2$ for planar reduced bodies. The construction is given by an explicit support function, and the proofs use only elementary support-function, width, area, and contact-point computations.
